name: Salamander Resort & Spa
positioning: Equestrian-themed countryside resort, called Salamander Middleburg on its official site, on 340 acres in Virginia's horse and wine country
best_for: Riders and families who want horses, trail rides and outdoor activities on site
Spa-focused weekend escapes from Washington, D.C.

facts.text: Salamander Middleburg sits on 340 acres in Virginia's horse and wine country.
The resort is part of Sheila C. Johnson's Salamander Collection.
Some of the equestrian-inspired decor was designed by owner Sheila Johnson, co-founder of BET.
Each room has outdoor space, either a balcony or a terrace.
Rooms come with luxe bathrobes, in-room coffee makers and nightly turndown service.
Guests can head down to the 22-stall horse barn for a trail ride.
Activities include riding, golf, tennis, fishing and a pool.
The resort has a putting green and tennis courts.
Children can ride horses, shoot arrows, splash in pools and zoom down zip lines.
Dining at the resort includes Harrimans Virginia Piedmont Grill.

highlights.text: The equestrian center has a pro-grade stable, nine paddocks and an outdoor arena.
The resort's spa covers 23,000 square feet.
Spa services are offered in rooms with adjacent private courtyards.
The Blue Ribbon Suite sits on a corner with expansive views of the Virginia landscape and a stone terrace.
Guests can take a treetop canopy tour.

considerations.text: The resort is in the small town of Middleburg, about an hour from Washington, D.C.
WhataHotel notes the rural location requires transportation for off-site activities.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Salamander Resort & Spa review
